notes: Known ledger (round-1/known.json) carries ~60 code-style rows on this chunk; all were suppressed, and only claims of different substance were kept. Cross-chunk: the cmd/configserver plist template's __PEEK_PORT__/__PEEK_CONTROL_PORT__/__PEEK_HOME_ARGS__ holes are filled by install.sh (another chunk), which this lane did not verify. Considered and dropped: passing Policy by value (the acdsl package passes Rule and other structs by value throughout) and WorktreeKindCount placed after a free function (it follows the file's existing section layout).

findings.fix: Capitalize the message after the prefix: "parsePolicy: Unknown mode %q" (L186) and "policyBase: No policy base resolves (tried %s) ..." (L218); update TestCheckPolicyUnresolvableBase's Contains to "No policy base resolves".
findings.claim: Two new error strings in policy.go start their <Message> lower-case — "parsePolicy: unknown mode %q" (L186) and "policyBase: no policy base resolves (tried %s) — ..." (L218) — while RULE-GOLANG-LOG-001 requires the message after the Function: prefix to begin with a capital letter and states this applies equally to error strings.
findings.evidence: Re-read policy.go L177-187 and L195-219 at head: both fmt.Errorf strings are new in this diff (policy.go is a new file) and start lower-case after the prefix. The acdsl package has three older lower-case instances (rule.go:191, rule.go:210, edit.go:22) — pre-existing, out of scope; the rule binds the added code. policy_test.go:288 asserts the lower-case substring and must move with the fix. Not in known.json (correctness-MAJ-65 concerns diagnostic content, not message casing).

findings.fix: Collapse the new third level: `if *peekStart && !startPeek(ctx, ...) { endpoint = ""; dashboardURL = "" }` inside the `*peekPort != 0` block, or move the peek wiring into a helper returning (endpoint, dashboardURL).
findings.claim: The added `if !startPeek(...) { endpoint = ""; dashboardURL = "" }` (L128-131) sits at the third control level (if *peekPort != 0 -> if *peekStart -> if !startPeek), while RULE-GOLANG-NEST-001 requires new code to be written to 2 levels.
findings.evidence: Re-read main.go L120-133 at head: L122 `if *peekPort != 0 {`, L127 `if *peekStart {`, L128 `if !startPeek(...) {` — the diff turned the former bare startPeek call into this third-level conditional. Known ledger rows on main.go (NIT-95 else-if, NIT-97 one-line call, NIT-96 param order, NIT-179/180) cover other lines/substance.

findings.fix: Replace the loop with a predicate: `hasOtherTrigger := slices.ContainsFunc(otherTriggerKeys, func(key string) bool { _, present := content[key]; return present })` and return `&scheduleInfo{Unscheduled: !hasOtherTrigger}`.
findings.claim: parseSchedule's new no-StartCalendarInterval branch nests three levels (if !ok -> for range otherTriggerKeys -> if present, L109-116); RULE-GOLANG-NEST-001 requires new code at 2 levels and explicitly counts range loops, which revive does not.
findings.evidence: Re-read plist.go L97-127 at head: L109 `if !ok {`, L111 `for _, key := range otherTriggerKeys {`, L112 `if _, present := content[key]; present {` — all three lines are added by this diff (base returned `nil, false, nil` directly). Known plist.go rows (NIT-61 placement, NIT-13 bool naming) are different substance.

findings.fix: Use kebab-case ids for the added/renamed cases: "unknown-state-ignored" (L47) and "probe-fixture-both-states-captured" (L26).
findings.claim: The case added in this diff is named "unknown state ignored" (L47) and the renamed fixture case "probe fixture: enabled and disabled labels both captured" (L26) — space- and colon-separated subtest ids, while RULE-GOLANG-TEST-006 requires kebab-case test case ids.
findings.evidence: Re-read launchctl_darwin_test.go L19-65 at head; diff shows L26 name rewritten and L46-49 case added in this change, both passed to t.Run(tc.name, ...). Known code-style-NIT-85-r1 flags the anonymous []struct table shape on this test — a different rule (STRUCT-006/TEST-001); converting the struct does not by itself fix the id casing, so this is not a trivial variant.

findings.fix: Turn TestCheckPolicyGatedVerifierAllowlist, TestCheckPolicyOverlay and TestCheckPolicyTaskContractExempt into testCase tables (_id, _expectedMessage/_expectedEmpty; basePolicyJson, workingFiles) with one append block per branch and a flat t.Run body.
findings.claim: Three new CheckPolicy tests (L228-244 allowlist default vs explicit, L246-261 overlay unsanctioned vs sanctioned, L263-278 task exemption on vs off) each script two branch scenarios sequentially in one body, rebuilding root and re-asserting by hand; RULE-GOLANG-TEST-014 requires table-driven tests when the method under test branches, one case per branch.
findings.evidence: Re-read policy_test.go L228-278 at head: each function reassigns root/diagnostics/err and repeats the CheckPolicy call + assertions for a second branch (classViolations allowlist branch, overlayViolations sanctioned branch, AllowTaskContracts branch in policy.go L89/L104/L167). Known policy_test rows cover TestLoadPolicy (NIT-68, NIT-158, NIT-12) and branch-commit coverage (tests-NIT-58); known NIT-16 is the same shape but in sessions_test.go — different file.
